main_text.l: fermones tuis actionibus semper respondet: Si
igitur ubi liber es, ubi quod velis potes: ubi etiā
vitę tuę profesio singularis famaq; verfatur, ibi
uno modo semper agas, ubi judicium tuum vis
existimem? Certè (opinor) in perpetua actio-
num, præsertim laudabiliū constantia. Hoc ufus
argumēto atq; judicio P. Ramus grammaticos
Donatū, Diomedem, rhetoras Quintilianum.
Ciceronē, philosophos & mathematicos Ari-
stolem, Euclidem de maximis rebus appella-
vit, & admonuit, magistroq; artium ufu fallaces
artium institutiones plerafq; refutavit. Ponatur
igitur hæc hypothesis atq; caussa: ibi Galeni ju-
dicium esse, ubi perpetuus Galeni usus, tanquā
nempe perpetua approbatio fuerit. Si quis igi-
tur de Galeni libris tam multis ullus sequatur
aliam methodum, aliamq; dispositionem quàm
Aristoteleam ab universalib. ad singularia: aut
si quis ejus liber totus & integer, artem aliquā
integram & totam, sola similitudine & dissimili
tudine artificiose componat (quę prima metho
dus ejus est) aut à specialissimis p media ad ge-
neralissimum artificiose progrediatur (quę co-
positio ejus est) aut sola consequentiū & repu-
gnantium consideratione artificiose constituat
(quæ methodus alicubi de tribus ei secūda est)
aut sola comparatione majorum, minorum, pa-
rium, aut eiusdem & diversi consideratione arti
ficiose cōficiat (quæ tertia) aut solo definitiōis
ordine deducat (quæ de tribus postremis ulti-
ma est) ego me(ajebat P.Ramus) in Galeni sen-
tentiā authoritatemq; servum sponte devoveā.
& quod

page.notes: Line numbers 5–30 are printed line-count markers in the left margin. Some words in the text are doubtful due to scan quality, notably in lines beginning "si quis ejus" and "artificiose". The final word line ("& quod") is incomplete at the page foot and continues on the next page.
